2. Apply to BPLIM for Quadros de Pessoal. It's free, open to any country, has the best fit and the standard AKM literature, and your advisor's signature is part of the application anyway.
3. If you're at an EU institution, also apply for the SIAB file or the MCVL. Otherwise, look for a coauthor or visiting position for Nordic, French or Brazilian data.

Search coverage: the dataset registries found little beyond the German LIAB records, so most candidates came from memory plus web search, then were checked. The Finnish statistics site, ICPSR and the UK Data Service catalogue blocked the automated checks.

The interactive shortlist, with filtering and an exportable access plan, is at `/private/tmp/e-gDF6oE/home/cwd/dataset-shortlist.html`.

graders.name: 01-recall-german-iab
graders.evidence:
Short answer: no openly downloadable linked employer-employee panel with real data exists in any country. You can start building and testing your AKM code today on simulated data and the IAB test files. The fastest real data are the **Veneto Worker Histories** and Spain's **MCVL** (a simple request form, probably a few weeks). Germany's **SIEED** is the best fit if you can wait a few months. Checked on 12 Nov 2026.

## What I assumed you need
- **R1 (must):** worker and employer identifiers that persist over time, so you can follow movers between firms.
- **R2 (must):** earnings for each job spell.
- **R3 (must):** at least 10 years of panel.
- **R4 (nice to have):** enough coverage that the connected set is large. Ideally that means nearly all workers, or all workers at the sampled firms.
- **R5 (nice to have):** a PhD student at a non-local institution can get it, ideally by remote access. I assumed you are not based in any of these countries. If you are, that country's registers jump up the list.

## Shortlist
| # | Dataset | Access | Size / coverage | Fit | Checked |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | **IAB SIEED** (Germany, 1975–2023) | Application to the IAB research data centre (FDZ) plus a use agreement signed by your institution. You run code remotely or on-site, never download. ~2–4 months | Full job histories of every worker ever employed at a ~1–1.5% sample of establishments | Strong | today |
| 2 | **MCVL** (Spain, 1980s–today) | Free request form to the Social Security directorate (DGOSS); you receive the data files. ~weeks | 4% of everyone with a Social Security record, with employer account codes | Strong (sample thin for firm effects) | today (eligibility of foreign institutions: from memory) |
| 3 | **Veneto Worker Histories** (Italy, 1975–2001) | Signed form emailed to the Fondazione Rodolfo Debenedetti (fRDB). ~weeks | All private firms in two provinces, with each worker followed wherever they move | Strong, but ends in 2001 | today |
| 4 | **Quadros de Pessoal via BPLIM** (Portugal, 1985–) | Application, confidentiality agreement signed by you and your supervisor, and CV. Free. BPLIM runs your code on the real data. May need a Banco de Portugal co-author. ~months | Nearly all private-sector workers and firms | Strong | today (co-author rule from a 2018 guide) |
| 5 | **Admin3 / Admin4** (Hungary, 2003–2017) | Only for researchers at the research centre that hosts it (KRTK), their co-authors, or PhD students they supervise. The new Admin4 has a remote level worth checking | 50% of the population, monthly | Strong | today |
| 6 | **US LEHD** via a Census research data centre | Proposal to Census with IRS and SSA approval, then security clearance. ~6–18 months | Nearly all workers, for participating states | Strong | today (timeline from memory) |
| 7 | **France: Panel tous salariés / DADS / BTS** via CASD | Approval by France's statistical secrecy committee, then paid access through CASD. Probably needs a French host | Panel covers 1/12 of workers | Strong | partly today |
| 8 | **UK ASHE** (SN 6689; NES back to 1975) | UK Data Service Secure Lab: Safe Researcher training plus an institutional application | 1% of workers | Partial: connected set too small | today |
| 9 | **Brazil RAIS identificada** | Formal cooperation agreement with the Labour Ministry, in practice through a Brazilian institution | All formal jobs since 1985 | Strong, hard to get | today |
| 10 | **Finland, FIONA remote access** | Agreement always goes through a Finnish organisation; per-module fees | Full population | Strong | partly (site unreachable today) |

## Details
**1. SIEED (Germany).** [Product page](https://fdz.iab.de/en/our-data-products/integrated-establishment-and-individual-data/sieed/). This is the dataset most clearly built for AKM-style work. For each sampled establishment it has the full job histories of everyone who ever worked there, plus the IAB's establishment panel. Access is "On-site Use / Remote Desktop Access including Remote Execution". The data centre has sites in the USA, UK and Canada and a remote-execution system called JoSuA. [Test data](https://doku.iab.de/fdz/siab/SIAB_Testdaten_en.pdf) let you write your code in advance.
- **Limits:** wages are top-coded at the social security ceiling, so you have to impute. You only see moves between sampled establishments. The full-population data used by Card, Heining and Kline (2013) requires a much heavier special project.
- **Alternative:** the related LIAB dataset is another German option on the same route.

**2. MCVL (Spain).** [Portal](https://portaldatos.seg-social.gob.es/mcvl).
- **Contents (portal, today):** each job spell is tied to an employer "código de cuenta de cotización". Contribution bases are recorded "mes a mes … a lo largo de su vida laboral" (month by month over the working life). A version with tax data adds uncensored earnings.
- **Who can apply:** public and private institutions, for non-commercial scientific use, free of charge. Juan José Dolado wrote in 2024 that some MCVL requests had been rejected that year.
- **Not confirmed:** whether institutions outside Spain qualify. Many non-Spanish researchers have used it, but that is from memory. Email DGOSS before you rely on it.
- **Limits:** with only 4% of workers you see few coworkers per firm. Plan on grouped firm effects (the BLM clustering approach) or keep to large firms.
- **Help:** [Diego Puga's MCVL code](https://diegopuga.org/data/mcvl/).
- **Related:** the same portal offers a firm-worker panel (PET) and remote research rooms.

**3. Veneto Worker Histories (Italy).** [fRDB page](https://www.frdb.org/en/dati/dati-inps-carriere-lavorative-in-veneto/). The only step is to "fill and sign the attached form and send it to info@frdb.org". The data are Italian social security records with worker and firm IDs and contract-level earnings. Kline, Saggio and Sølvsten used it for their [leave-out AKM estimator](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1806.01494). Jaime Arellano-Bover keeps [practical notes](https://www.jarellanobover.com/veneto-workers-histories-dataset-additional-resources). The catch is that it ends in 2001.

**4. Quadros de Pessoal (Portugal).** [BPLIM access page](https://bplim.bportugal.pt/content/access-0). This is the data behind Card, Cardoso and Kline (2016). Outside researchers write code on pseudo-data and BPLIM staff run it on the real data. A [2018 guide](https://cicee.autonoma.pt/wp-content/uploads/2024/03/BPlim_Guide_for_Researchers_v2018sep26.pdf) limits QP to Banco de Portugal researchers and joint projects with them. Check the current Guide for Researchers.

**5–10.** Sources for the rest:
- Hungary: [Admin3 page](https://adatbank.krtk.mta.hu/en/2020/02/) and the [Admin4 working paper](https://kti.krtk.hu/wp-content/uploads/2026/02/KRTKKTIWP202601.pdf)
- US: [LEHD restricted data](https://www.census.gov/programs-surveys/ces/data/restricted-use-data/lehd-data.html). Proposals must state a benefit to the LEHD programme.
- France: [CASD record](http://datapresentation.casd.eu/10.34724/CASD.21.5012.V1)
- UK: [ASHE catalogue entry](https://datacatalogue.ukdataservice.ac.uk/studies/study/6689). The tool could not check this page automatically.
- Brazil: [gov.br request page](https://www.gov.br/pt-br/servicos/solicitar-acesso-aos-dados-identificados-rais-e-caged)
- Finland: [FIONA guide](https://guides.stat.fi/remote-access-to-research-data/application-process-and-agreement-practices)

## What you can start today
- **[PyTwoWay](https://github.com/tlamadon/pytwoway/) / [BipartitePandas](https://github.com/tlamadon/bipartitepandas).** `pip install pytwoway`. It simulates worker-firm data with known true effects and runs AKM with standard bias corrections (KSS, BLM). Build and validate your whole within/between decomposition on it. [The ABC of AKM](https://lamadon.com/paper/akm-abc.pdf) is a good companion.
- **IAB test data.** Write your code in the format the German research data centre expects, so it runs on SIEED as soon as you are approved.
- **This week:** email fRDB for the Veneto data and DGOSS for the MCVL. Both are cheap, and Veneto in particular gives you real data on a full set of firms within weeks.

## Not recommended
- **Public RAIS (Brazil):** no worker or firm identifiers.
- **PSID, NLSY, SOEP:** no coworker structure, so firm effects can't be identified.
- **LEHD public products (QWI, LODES):** aggregate tables only.
- **SIAB:** a 2% sample of workers, which makes the connected set too thin. Use SIEED or LIAB instead.

## What I could not check
- Whether the MCVL accepts foreign institutions (the portal blocked direct reading).
- Whether foreign researchers can use the French data.
- Austria (the ASSD and the new Austrian Micro Data Center), Denmark, Norway, Sweden, the Netherlands and Canada (CEEDD), apart from a quick search on Austria that didn't settle anything. From memory, all of them need an institution based in that country.

## Next step
For the dissertation, aim for **SIEED** (or Portugal's QP if a Banco de Portugal co-author is realistic) for the main analysis. Use **Veneto** or **MCVL** to get going within weeks, and develop on PyTwoWay in the meantime. Talk to your advisor early, because the German, Portuguese and Hungarian routes all go faster with an institutional agreement or a co-author.

I've saved an interactive version of this shortlist, with filters and an exportable access plan, at `/private/tmp/e-qPJ7dL/home/cwd/dataset-shortlist.html`.

Sources: [MCVL portal](https://portaldatos.seg-social.gob.es/mcvl) · [Dolado, Nada es Gratis](https://nadaesgratis.es/dolado/pesadilla-con-el-pet) · [FDZ SIEED](https://fdz.iab.de/en/our-data-products/integrated-establishment-and-individual-data/sieed/) · [FDZ access](https://fdz.iab.de/en/data-access/on-site-use/) · [fRDB VWH](https://www.frdb.org/en/dati/dati-inps-carriere-lavorative-in-veneto/) · [BPLIM access](https://bplim.bportugal.pt/content/access-0) · [KRTK Admin3](https://adatbank.krtk.mta.hu/en/2020/02/) · [LEHD](https://www.census.gov/programs-surveys/ces/data/restricted-use-data/lehd-data.html) · [CASD BTS](http://datapresentation.casd.eu/10.34724/CASD.21.5012.V1) · [UKDS ASHE](https://datacatalogue.ukdataservice.ac.uk/studies/study/6689) · [RAIS identificada](https://www.gov.br/pt-br/servicos/solicitar-acesso-aos-dados-identificados-rais-e-caged) · [Statistics Finland FIONA](https://guides.stat.fi/remote-access-to-research-data/application-process-and-agreement-practices) · [PyTwoWay](https://github.com/tlamadon/pytwoway/)

|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | **IAB SIEED** (Germany, 1975–2023) | Application to the IAB research data centre (FDZ) plus a use agreement signed by your institution. | 3 | **Veneto Worker Histories** (Italy, 1975–2001) | Signed form emailed to the Fondazione Rodolfo Debenedetti (fRDB). ~weeks | All private firms in two provinces, with each worker followed wherever they move | Strong, but ends in 2001 | today |
| 4 | **Quadros de Pessoal via BPLIM** (Portugal, 1985–) | Application, confidentiality agreement signed by you and your supervisor, and CV. Free. BPLIM runs your code on the real data. | 7 | **France: Panel tous salariés / DADS / BTS** via CASD | Approval by France's statistical secrecy committee, then paid access through CASD. Probably needs a French host | Panel covers 1/12 of workers | Strong | partly today |

| 7 | **France: Panel tous salariés / DADS / BTS** via CASD | Approval by France's statistical secrecy committee, then paid access through CASD. Probably needs a French host | Panel covers 1/12 of workers | Strong | partly today |
| 8 | **UK ASHE** (SN 6689; NES back to 1975) | UK Data Service Secure Lab: Safe Researcher training plus an institutional application | 1% of workers | Partial: connected set too small | today |
| 9 | **Brazil RAIS identificada** | Formal cooperation agreement with the Labour Ministry, in practice through a Brazilian institution | All formal jobs since 1985 | Strong, hard to get | today |
| 10 | **Finland, FIONA remote access** | Agreement always goes through a Finnish organisation; per-module fees | Full population | Strong | partly (site unreachable today) |

## Details
**1. SIEED (Germany).** [Product page](https://fdz.iab.de/en/our-data-products/integrated-establishment-and-individual-data/sieed/). This is the dataset most clearly built for AKM-style work. For each sampled establishment it has the full job histories of everyone who ever worked there, plus the IAB's establishment panel. Access is "On-site Use / Remote Desktop Access including Remote Execution". The data centre has sites in the USA, UK and Canada and a remote-execution system called JoSuA. [Test data](https://doku.iab.de/fdz/siab/SIAB_Testdaten_en.pdf) let you write your code in advance.
- **Limits:** wages are top-coded at the social security ceiling, so you have to impute. You only see moves between sampled establishments. The full-population data used by Card, Heining and Kline (2013) requires a much heavier special project.
- **Alternative:** the related LIAB dataset is another German option on the same route.

**2. MCVL (Spain).** [Portal](https://portaldatos.seg-social.gob.es/mcvl).
- **Contents (portal, today):** each job spell is tied to an employer "código de cuenta de cotización". Contribution bases are recorded "mes a mes … a lo largo de su vida laboral" (month by month over the working life). A version with tax data adds uncensored earnings.
- **Who can apply:** public and private institutions, for non-commercial scientific use, free of charge. Juan José Dolado wrote in 2024 that some MCVL requests had been rejected that year.
- **Not confirmed:** whether institutions outside Spain qualify. Many non-Spanish researchers have used it, but that is from memory. Email DGOSS before you rely on it.
- **Limits:** with only 4% of workers you see few coworkers per firm. Plan on grouped firm effects (the BLM clustering approach) or keep to large firms.
- **Help:** [Diego Puga's MCVL code](https://diegopuga.org/data/mcvl/).
- **Related:** the same portal offers a firm-worker panel (PET) and remote research rooms.

**3. Veneto Worker Histories (Italy).** [fRDB page](https://www.frdb.org/en/dati/dati-inps-carriere-lavorative-in-veneto/). The only step is to "fill and sign the attached form and send it to info@frdb.org". The data are Italian social security records with worker and firm IDs and contract-level earnings. Kline, Saggio and Sølvsten used it for their [leave-out AKM estimator](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1806.01494). Jaime Arellano-Bover keeps [practical notes](https://www.jarellanobover.com/veneto-workers-histories-dataset-additional-resources). The catch is that it ends in 2001.

**4. Quadros de Pessoal (Portugal).** [BPLIM access page](https://bplim.bportugal.pt/content/access-0). This is the data behind Card, Cardoso and Kline (2016). Outside researchers write code on pseudo-data and BPLIM staff run it on the real data. A [2018 guide](https://cicee.autonoma.pt/wp-content/uploads/2024/03/BPlim_Guide_for_Researchers_v2018sep26.pdf) limits QP to Banco de Portugal researchers and joint projects with them. Check the current Guide for Researchers.

**5–10.** Sources for the rest:
- Hungary: [Admin3 page](https://adatbank.krtk.mta.hu/en/2020/02/) and the [Admin4 working paper](https://kti.krtk.hu/wp-content/uploads/2026/02/KRTKKTIWP202601.pdf)
- US: [LEHD restricted data](https://www.census.gov/programs-surveys/ces/data/restricted-use-data/lehd-data.html). Proposals must state a benefit to the LEHD programme.
- France: [CASD record](http://datapresentation.casd.eu/10.34724/CASD.21.5012.V1)
- UK: [ASHE catalogue entry](https://datacatalogue.ukdataservice.ac.uk/studies/study/6689). The tool could not check this page automatically.
- Brazil: [gov.br request page](https://www.gov.br/pt-br/servicos/solicitar-acesso-aos-dados-identificados-rais-e-caged)
- Finland: [FIONA guide](https://guides.stat.fi/remote-access-to-research-data/application-process-and-agreement-practices)

## What you can start today
- **[PyTwoWay](https://github.com/tlamadon/pytwoway/) / [BipartitePandas](https://github.com/tlamadon/bipartitepandas).** `pip install pytwoway`. It simulates worker-firm data with known true effects and runs AKM with standard bias corrections (KSS, BLM). Build and validate your whole within/between decomposition on it. [The ABC of AKM](https://lamadon.com/paper/akm-abc.pdf) is a good companion.
- **IAB test data.** Write your code in the format the German research data centre expects, so it runs on SIEED as soon as you are approved.
- **This week:** email fRDB for the Veneto data and DGOSS for the MCVL. Both are cheap, and Veneto in particular gives you real data on a full set of firms within weeks.

## Not recommended
- **Public RAIS (Brazil):** no worker or firm identifiers.
- **PSID, NLSY, SOEP:** no coworker structure, so firm effects can't be identified.
- **LEHD public products (QWI, LODES):** aggregate tables only.
- **SIAB:** a 2% sample of workers, which makes the connected set too thin. Use SIEED or LIAB instead.

## What I could not check
- Whether the MCVL accepts foreign institutions (the portal blocked direct reading).
- Whether foreign researchers can use the French data.
- Austria (the ASSD and the new Austrian Micro Data Center), Denmark, Norway, Sweden, the Netherlands and Canada (CEEDD), apart from a quick search on Austria that didn't settle anything. From memory, all of them need an institution based in that country.

## Next step
For the dissertation, aim for **SIEED** (or Portugal's QP if a Banco de Portugal co-author is realistic) for the main analysis. Use **Veneto** or **MCVL** to get going within weeks, and develop on PyTwoWay in the meantime. Talk to your advisor early, because the German, Portuguese and Hungarian routes all go faster with an institutional agreement or a co-author.

I've saved an interactive version of this shortlist, with filters and an exportable access plan, at `/private/tmp/e-qPJ7dL/home/cwd/dataset-shortlist.html`.

Sources: [MCVL portal](https://portaldatos.seg-social.gob.es/mcvl) · [Dolado, Nada es Gratis](https://nadaesgratis.es/dolado/pesadilla-con-el-pet) · [FDZ SIEED](https://fdz.iab.de/en/our-data-products/integrated-establishment-and-individual-data/sieed/) · [FDZ access](https://fdz.iab.de/en/data-access/on-site-use/) · [fRDB VWH](https://www.frdb.org/en/dati/dati-inps-carriere-lavorative-in-veneto/) · [BPLIM access](https://bplim.bportugal.pt/content/access-0) · [KRTK Admin3](https://adatbank.krtk.mta.hu/en/2020/02/) · [LEHD](https://www.census.gov/programs-surveys/ces/data/restricted-use-data/lehd-data.html) · [CASD BTS](http://datapresentation.casd.eu/10.34724/CASD.21.5012.V1) · [UKDS ASHE](https://datacatalogue.ukdataservice.ac.uk/studies/study/6689) · [RAIS identificada](https://www.gov.br/pt-br/servicos/solicitar-acesso-aos-dados-identificados-rais-e-caged) · [Statistics Finland FIONA](https://guides.stat.fi/remote-access-to-research-data/application-process-and-agreement-practices) · [PyTwoWay](https://github.com/tlamadon/pytwoway/)

graders.name: 01-recall-german-iab
graders.evidence:
No dataset like this is openly downloadable. In every country I checked, the employer ID is exactly what gets removed from the public files, so every option below needs an application. The quickest are **Spain's MCVL** and the **Veneto worker histories** (a form, then probably weeks). Germany and Portugal take a few months. Brazil, the US and Hungary are slower or need a local partner. What you can start on **today** is your full AKM pipeline on simulated data with **pytwoway**, and on Germany's free practice files, which match the real LIAB layout.

Checked 2026-11-12. "Confirmed" means I read it on the data owner's page today; "from memory" means I couldn't confirm it.

## What I assumed you need
- **R1 (must):** a worker ID and an employer ID that are consistent across workers and years. Without both, you can't estimate firm effects from people who change jobs.
- **R2 (must):** earnings for each job spell.
- **R3 (must):** at least 10 years.
- **R6 (must):** a PhD student can get it. I assumed you may not be based in that country.
- **Nice to have:** near-complete coverage of a firm's workers, so many firms are connected through movers (R4), and earnings that aren't capped at a ceiling (R5).

## Shortlist
| # | Dataset | Access | Years | Fit | Checked |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Spain: MCVL, 4% sample of social security records (Social Security agency) | Application, free, files sent to you; weeks | 1980s–present | Strong (small sample per firm) | today, plus some from memory |
| 2 | Germany: IAB LIAB longitudinal model | Application and agreement; code is run for you or on-site; months | 1975–2021/2024 | Strong | today |
| 3 | Portugal: Quadros de Pessoal, via Banco de Portugal's data lab (BPLIM) | Application, confidentiality agreement, secure remote server; months | mid-1980s onward | Strong | access rules today, contents from memory |
| 4 | Italy: Veneto Worker Histories (VWH) | Signed form emailed to the distributor; probably weeks | 1975–2001 | Strong, but old and regional | today |
| 5 | Brazil: identified RAIS | Cooperation agreement between an institution and the Labour Ministry; months | 1985–present | Strong | today |
| 6 | US: LEHD, through a Census research data center | Proposal, sworn status, several agency approvals; 6–12+ months | ~2000 onward | Strong | today |
| 7 | Germany: SIAB, on-site version | Same process as LIAB | 1975–2023 | Partial (2% worker sample) | today |
| 8 | Hungary: Admin3 (KRTK Databank) | Needs a KRTK coauthor | 2003–2017 | Partial | today |
| 9 | pytwoway simulated data | Open, `pip install` | any | For building code only | today |

## Details

**1. MCVL (Spain).** [portaldatos.seg-social.gob.es/mcvl](https://portaldatos.seg-social.gob.es/mcvl)
- **What it is:** a 4% random sample of everyone with any link to Spanish Social Security. Each person's full work history is included, back as far as computer records go. Monthly contribution earnings are included (confirmed on the portal). From memory, each job also carries an anonymised employer account and a firm tax ID.
- **How to get it:** download the application form and researcher form from the portal. Request the version **with tax data**, because the social security earnings are capped at the top and bottom and the tax data aren't. The Social Security directorate (DGOSS) approves requests from institutions doing non-commercial research.
- **Use this code:** [Diego Puga's MCVL code](https://diegopuga.org/data/mcvl/) for building the panel.
- **Watch out for:**
  - With 4% of workers, most firms have only 0–2 sampled employees. Firm effects will be noisy and the connected set small, so plan on bias-corrected (KSS-type) estimates.
  - Approval isn't automatic. Juan José Dolado reported two rejections in 2024 ([Nada es Gratis](https://nadaesgratis.es/dolado/pesadilla-con-el-pet)).
  - From memory, foreign universities can apply. Confirm this by email.

**2. LIAB longitudinal model (Germany).** [FDZ page](https://fdz.iab.de/en/int_bd_pd/linked-employer-employee-data-of-the-iab-liab-liab-longitudinal-model-1975-2021-version-1/)
- **What it is:** firms sampled through the IAB's annual firm survey, with complete employment histories of their workers.
- **Who can apply:** non-German researchers on the same terms as Germans. About half of current projects include collaborators abroad.
- **How you work with it:** you can't download it. You submit code that FDZ staff run for you (their remote-execution system, JoSuA), or you work on-site in Germany or at a guest site: Michigan, Berkeley, Harvard, Princeton, UCLA, Cornell, London, Essex, Vancouver ([locations](https://fdz.iab.de/en/appointment-locations-and-fdz-online-calendar/)).
- **Watch out for:**
  - Earnings are capped at the social security ceiling (imputation is standard).
  - The 7524 page says full employment histories are provided only for firms with fewer than 50 employees.
  - Sites outside the EU add extra anonymisation that can't be undone.
  - FDZ also publishes ready-made AKM firm effects you can merge in ([method report 03/2025](https://doku.iab.de/fdz/reporte/2025/MR_03-25_EN.pdf)).
- **Key paper:** Card, Heining & Kline (2013), [doi:10.3386/w18522](https://doi.org/10.3386/w18522).

**3. Quadros de Pessoal (Portugal).**
- **What it is (from memory):** a mandatory annual census of all private-sector employers and their workers, without an earnings cap. It's the data behind Card, Cardoso & Kline (2016).
- **How to get it (confirmed on [BPLIM's access page](https://bplim.bportugal.pt/content/access-0)):** application form, CV and confidentiality agreement. It's free and for research only. You build code on practice data, then work on BPLIM's external server. You can't transfer files yourself; outputs are sent to you by email.
- **Not confirmed:** whether outside researchers also need approval from the Labour Ministry, which supplies the data under a protocol ([2018 guide](https://cicee.autonoma.pt/wp-content/uploads/2024/03/BPlim_Guide_for_Researchers_v2018sep26.pdf)).

**4. Veneto Worker Histories (Italy).** [FRDB page](https://www.frdb.org/en/dati/dati-inps-carriere-lavorative-in-veneto/)
- **What it is:** every private-sector firm in Treviso and Vicenza and all their workers, followed through their whole careers, 1975–2001.
- **How to get it:** sign the form on that page and email it to info@frdb.org. The page doesn't say who is eligible or how the data are delivered.
- **Watch out for:** it ends in 2001, so it says little about recent trends.
- **Key paper:** Kline, Saggio & Sølvsten's leave-out (KSS) method was developed on this data ([arXiv 1806.01494](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1806.01494)).

**5. Identified RAIS (Brazil).** [Request page](https://www.gov.br/pt-br/servicos/solicitar-acesso-aos-dados-identificados-rais-e-caged)
- **What it is:** every formal job in Brazil, with worker and firm IDs.
- **How to get it:** the request must come from an *organisation*, not a person. It signs a cooperation agreement with the Labour Ministry's statistics office, and each user signs a confidentiality agreement.
- **In practice:** this is hard for a foreign university. It's worth asking whether your department or advisor already holds an agreement.

**6. LEHD (US).** [Census LEHD page](https://www.census.gov/programs-surveys/ces/data/restricted-use-data/lehd-data.html)
- **What it is:** quarterly earnings for nearly all jobs in participating states, mostly from 2000 on, with no hours.
- **How to get it:**
  - A proposal through a Federal Statistical Research Data Center (FSRDC), with your advisor as co-PI. It must show a benefit to the Census Bureau.
  - Special Sworn Status, and approvals from the IRS and Social Security for some files.
- **Rules:** you must have lived in the US for 3 of the last 5 years, results must cover at least 3 states, and all work happens inside an FSRDC.

**7–8.** The on-site **SIAB** has the IDs but samples only 2% of workers, so it's weak for firm effects. **Admin3** is a 50% population sample with monthly employer links, but only for KRTK researchers and their coauthors. A newer Admin4 may offer wider access tiers.

**9. Start today.** [pytwoway](https://github.com/tlamadon/pytwoway):
- `pip install pytwoway`
- Simulate worker-firm data with chosen sorting and mobility using `bpd.SimBipartite`.
- Estimate AKM with plug-in, homoskedastic and KSS corrections using `tw.FEEstimator(he=True)`.
- Also download FDZ's free LIAB practice data in Stata format from the LIAB page. The values are random but the variables match the real data, so code written on it will carry over to remote execution.

## Known, not confirmed
- **Finland** (FOLK employment modules through the FIONA remote system): full-population data, but the agreement must be with a Finnish organisation and there are fees. The site blocked automated checks.
- **Not checked at all:**
  - Denmark, Sweden and Norway registers: these normally need a local institution.
  - France's DADS / Panel tous salariés, accessed through its secure research environment (CASD).
  - Austria's social security database (ASSD), UK ASHE, Canada CEEDD, Italy's INPS programme for visiting researchers (VisitINPS), Taiwan, Chile, Mexico (IMSS).

## Not recommended
- **PSID and NLSY:** employer IDs aren't shared across respondents, so firm effects can't be estimated.
- **SIAB download version and public RAIS:** both are free, but neither has employer IDs that link workers.

## Next step
1. This week, build the pipeline on pytwoway simulated data.
2. Submit the MCVL application (with tax data) and the VWH form now. Both are cheap.
3. Start the FDZ LIAB application with your advisor, since it's the strongest long-run option. If Portugal is attractive, write to BPLIM at the same time to ask about Quadros de Pessoal terms for outside researchers.

Interactive page: `/private/tmp/e-jvrm6C/home/cwd/dataset-shortlist.html` (data in `dataset-scout/shortlist.json`)

- **R1 (must):** a worker ID and an employer ID that are consistent across workers and years. Without both, you can't estimate firm effects from people who change jobs.
- **R2 (must):** earnings for each job spell.
- **R3 (must):** at least 10 years.
- **R6 (must):** a PhD student can get it. I assumed you may not be based in that country.
- **Nice to have:** near-complete coverage of a firm's workers, so many firms are connected through movers (R4), and earnings that aren't capped at a ceiling (R5).

## Shortlist
| # | Dataset | Access | Years | Fit | Checked |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Spain: MCVL, 4% sample of social security records (Social Security agency) | Application, free, files sent to you; weeks | 1980s–present | Strong (small sample per firm) | today, plus some from memory |
| 2 | Germany: IAB LIAB longitudinal model | Application and agreement; code is run for you or on-site; months | 1975–2021/2024 | Strong | today |
| 3 | Portugal: Quadros de Pessoal, via Banco de Portugal's data lab (BPLIM) | Application, confidentiality agreement, secure remote server; months | mid-1980s onward | Strong | access rules today, contents from memory |
| 4 | Italy: Veneto Worker Histories (VWH) | Signed form emailed to the distributor; probably weeks | 1975–2001 | Strong, but old and regional | today |
| 5 | Brazil: identified RAIS | Cooperation agreement between an institution and the Labour Ministry; months | 1985–present | Strong | today |
| 6 | US: LEHD, through a Census research data center | Proposal, sworn status, several agency approvals; 6–12+ months | ~2000 onward | Strong | today |
| 7 | Germany: SIAB, on-site version | Same process as LIAB | 1975–2023 | Partial (2% worker sample) | today |
| 8 | Hungary: Admin3 (KRTK Databank) | Needs a KRTK coauthor | 2003–2017 | Partial | today |
| 9 | pytwoway simulated data | Open, `pip install` | any | For building code only | today |

## Details

**1. MCVL (Spain).** [portaldatos.seg-social.gob.es/mcvl](https://portaldatos.seg-social.gob.es/mcvl)
- **What it is:** a 4% random sample of everyone with any link to Spanish Social Security. Each person's full work history is included, back as far as computer records go. Monthly contribution earnings are included (confirmed on the portal). From memory, each job also carries an anonymised employer account and a firm tax ID.
- **How to get it:** download the application form and researcher form from the portal. Request the version **with tax data**, because the social security earnings are capped at the top and bottom and the tax data aren't. The Social Security directorate (DGOSS) approves requests from institutions doing non-commercial research.
- **Use this code:** [Diego Puga's MCVL code](https://diegopuga.org/data/mcvl/) for building the panel.
- **Watch out for:**
  - With 4% of workers, most firms have only 0–2 sampled employees. Firm effects will be noisy and the connected set small, so plan on bias-corrected (KSS-type) estimates.
  - Approval isn't automatic. Juan José Dolado reported two rejections in 2024 ([Nada es Gratis](https://nadaesgratis.es/dolado/pesadilla-con-el-pet)).
  - From memory, foreign universities can apply. Confirm this by email.

**2. LIAB longitudinal model (Germany).** [FDZ page](https://fdz.iab.de/en/int_bd_pd/linked-employer-employee-data-of-the-iab-liab-liab-longitudinal-model-1975-2021-version-1/)
- **What it is:** firms sampled through the IAB's annual firm survey, with complete employment histories of their workers.
- **Who can apply:** non-German researchers on the same terms as Germans. About half of current projects include collaborators abroad.
- **How you work with it:** you can't download it. You submit code that FDZ staff run for you (their remote-execution system, JoSuA), or you work on-site in Germany or at a guest site: Michigan, Berkeley, Harvard, Princeton, UCLA, Cornell, London, Essex, Vancouver ([locations](https://fdz.iab.de/en/appointment-locations-and-fdz-online-calendar/)).
- **Watch out for:**
  - Earnings are capped at the social security ceiling (imputation is standard).
  - The 7524 page says full employment histories are provided only for firms with fewer than 50 employees.
  - Sites outside the EU add extra anonymisation that can't be undone.
  - FDZ also publishes ready-made AKM firm effects you can merge in ([method report 03/2025](https://doku.iab.de/fdz/reporte/2025/MR_03-25_EN.pdf)).
- **Key paper:** Card, Heining & Kline (2013), [doi:10.3386/w18522](https://doi.org/10.3386/w18522).

**3. Quadros de Pessoal (Portugal).**
- **What it is (from memory):** a mandatory annual census of all private-sector employers and their workers, without an earnings cap. It's the data behind Card, Cardoso & Kline (2016).
- **How to get it (confirmed on [BPLIM's access page](https://bplim.bportugal.pt/content/access-0)):** application form, CV and confidentiality agreement. It's free and for research only. You build code on practice data, then work on BPLIM's external server. You can't transfer files yourself; outputs are sent to you by email.
- **Not confirmed:** whether outside researchers also need approval from the Labour Ministry, which supplies the data under a protocol ([2018 guide](https://cicee.autonoma.pt/wp-content/uploads/2024/03/BPlim_Guide_for_Researchers_v2018sep26.pdf)).

**4. Veneto Worker Histories (Italy).** [FRDB page](https://www.frdb.org/en/dati/dati-inps-carriere-lavorative-in-veneto/)
- **What it is:** every private-sector firm in Treviso and Vicenza and all their workers, followed through their whole careers, 1975–2001.
- **How to get it:** sign the form on that page and email it to info@frdb.org. The page doesn't say who is eligible or how the data are delivered.
- **Watch out for:** it ends in 2001, so it says little about recent trends.
- **Key paper:** Kline, Saggio & Sølvsten's leave-out (KSS) method was developed on this data ([arXiv 1806.01494](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1806.01494)).

**5. Identified RAIS (Brazil).** [Request page](https://www.gov.br/pt-br/servicos/solicitar-acesso-aos-dados-identificados-rais-e-caged)
- **What it is:** every formal job in Brazil, with worker and firm IDs.
- **How to get it:** the request must come from an *organisation*, not a person. It signs a cooperation agreement with the Labour Ministry's statistics office, and each user signs a confidentiality agreement.
- **In practice:** this is hard for a foreign university. It's worth asking whether your department or advisor already holds an agreement.

**6. LEHD (US).** [Census LEHD page](https://www.census.gov/programs-surveys/ces/data/restricted-use-data/lehd-data.html)
- **What it is:** quarterly earnings for nearly all jobs in participating states, mostly from 2000 on, with no hours.
- **How to get it:**
  - A proposal through a Federal Statistical Research Data Center (FSRDC), with your advisor as co-PI. It must show a benefit to the Census Bureau.
  - Special Sworn Status, and approvals from the IRS and Social Security for some files.
- **Rules:** you must have lived in the US for 3 of the last 5 years, results must cover at least 3 states, and all work happens inside an FSRDC.

**7–8.** The on-site **SIAB** has the IDs but samples only 2% of workers, so it's weak for firm effects. **Admin3** is a 50% population sample with monthly employer links, but only for KRTK researchers and their coauthors. A newer Admin4 may offer wider access tiers.

**9. Start today.** [pytwoway](https://github.com/tlamadon/pytwoway):
- `pip install pytwoway`
- Simulate worker-firm data with chosen sorting and mobility using `bpd.SimBipartite`.
- Estimate AKM with plug-in, homoskedastic and KSS corrections using `tw.FEEstimator(he=True)`.

- **Finland** (FOLK employment modules through the FIONA remote system): full-population data, but the agreement must be with a Finnish organisation and there are fees. The site blocked automated checks.
- **Not checked at all:**
  - Denmark, Sweden and Norway registers: these normally need a local institution.
  - France's DADS / Panel tous salariés, accessed through its secure research environment (CASD).
  - Austria's social security database (ASSD), UK ASHE, Canada CEEDD, Italy's INPS programme for visiting researchers (VisitINPS), Taiwan, Chile, Mexico (IMSS).

## Not recommended
- **PSID and NLSY:** employer IDs aren't shared across respondents, so firm effects can't be estimated.
- **SIAB download version and public RAIS:** both are free, but neither has employer IDs that link workers.

## Next step
1. This week, build the pipeline on pytwoway simulated data.
2. Submit the MCVL application (with tax data) and the VWH form now. Both are cheap.
3. Start the FDZ LIAB application with your advisor, since it's the strongest long-run option. If Portugal is attractive, write to BPLIM at the same time to ask about Quadros de Pessoal terms for outside researchers.

graders.name: 01-recall-german-iab
graders.evidence:
I checked the access rules for Germany, Portugal, and Brazil online this session. Everything else below comes from what I already know, so confirm details with each data provider before you plan around them.

## Short answer

You can't legally get worker-level linked employer-employee wage data with firm IDs immediately anywhere. Every dataset good enough for AKM needs an application. What you can do right away is build and test your whole pipeline on test data and simulated data, so you're ready to run it the day access comes through.

## Main options, roughly from most to least feasible for a PhD student

**1. Germany: IAB/FDZ (LIAB longitudinal model, or the full-population establishment and worker data behind Card–Heining–Kline 2013)**
- **Why it fits:** It's the standard AKM dataset. The latest longitudinal model covers 1975–2021 ([FDZ](https://fdz.iab.de/en/int_bd_pd/linked-employer-employee-data-of-the-iab-liab-liab-longitudinal-model-1975-2021-version-1/)).
- **What access takes:**
  - Your institution has to do independent scientific research and sit in the EU or a country with GDPR "adequacy" status. You can't apply as a freelancer.
  - LIAB is not distributed as a file. You work on-site, then usually move to remote access, or you use remote execution: you send Stata scripts and FDZ checks the output before releasing it ([FDZ access](https://fdz.iab.de/en/data-access/on-site-use/), [MIT handbook chapter](https://admindatahandbook.mit.edu/book/v1.1/iab.html)).
  - FDZ also has guest workplaces in the US, Canada, and the UK, which helps if you're based outside Europe.
  - Access is free. Approval typically takes a few months, though that's my estimate.
- **Caveat:** SIAB, the easier-to-get 2% worker sample, is too sparse within firms for credible firm effects (limited mobility bias). For AKM you want LIAB or the larger custom extracts.

**2. Portugal: Quadros de Pessoal**
- **Why it fits:** It's a near-census of private-sector employees with worker and firm IDs from the mid-1980s on, and it's used widely in AKM papers.
- **What access takes:**
  - The usual route is Banco de Portugal's BPLIM lab. Access is free. You apply with a project description, a CV, and a confidentiality agreement.
  - You write code on modified, non-valid data, and BPLIM staff run it on the real data and email you the outputs ([BPLIM access](https://bplim.bportugal.pt/content/access-0)).
  - An older BPLIM guide (2018) said QP was limited to Bank researchers and their co-authors. Ask BPLIM directly whether a solo external researcher can get it now. If not, the alternative is applying to the Labour Ministry's statistics office (GEP/MTSSS), or finding a co-author.

**3. Brazil: RAIS**
- **Why it fits:** It's a huge formal-sector census, popular for AKM and inequality work (e.g., Alvarez et al. 2018).
- **What access takes:**
  - The public RAIS downloads (and the Base dos Dados BigQuery mirror) have no worker identifiers, so you **can't follow workers or run AKM with them**.
  - The identified RAIS requires a formal application to the Labour Ministry (MTE) under Portaria 671/2021. You need an official letter from your institution and a CPF or foreign ID, and you sign a cooperation agreement ([gov.br service](https://www.gov.br/pt-br/servicos/solicitar-acesso-aos-dados-identificados-rais-e-caged)).
  - People report it's possible but slow and unpredictable, and it has gotten harder since Brazil's data protection law (LGPD).

**4. United States: LEHD, through the Census secure research centers (FSRDCs)**
- **What access takes:**
  - You write a full proposal that has to show a benefit to Census, get Special Sworn Status (background check), and work at or through a secure research center.
  - For LEHD, the states that supply the data also have to approve the project.
  - Approval commonly takes 6–12 months or more, and you can't export anything without a disclosure review.
- **Verdict:** It works if your university has a center and your advisor or a co-author already has a project you can join. It's risky as a solo second-year route.

**5. Nordic registers (Denmark, Sweden, Norway, Finland)**
- **Why they fit:** The data are excellent: full population, long panels.
- **What access takes:** You almost always need to be affiliated with an authorized institution in that country, such as a university or central bank. In practice you get in through a local co-author or a research visit.

**6. Others**
- **France:** DADS / Panel Tous Salariés via CASD. You need committee approval, and there are fees.
- **Austria:** ASSD, accessed through Austrian university contacts.
- **Italy:** INPS through VisitINPS, which requires an on-site stay. Also the Veneto Worker History, which is older (roughly 1975–2001) but historically easier to request.
- **Canada:** CEEDD through Statistics Canada's research data centres.
- **UK:** ASHE via the ONS Secure Research Service. It's a 1% worker sample, which is thin for firm effects, and access is easiest from a UK institution.

## What you can start on right away

1. **IAB test data.** FDZ publishes Stata test datasets that have the same structure as SIAB and LIAB. You can write and debug your full sample construction (spells, connected set, AKM, variance decomposition) on them now. They're built so you can prepare remote-execution code.
2. **Simulated data.** The `pytwoway` package (Lamadon and co-authors) simulates worker–firm networks and estimates AKM, KSS leave-out bias correction, and the Bonhomme–Lamadon–Manresa (BLM) model. In Stata, `reghdfe` handles the two-way fixed effects. With these you can learn how limited mobility bias behaves and validate your decomposition code before you see real data.
3. **Replicate published decompositions** from public results tables, such as Song et al. 2019 "Firming Up Inequality" and Card–Heining–Kline 2013. Then you'll know exactly which outputs you need cleared for release.
4. **Avoid commercial career-history data** (Revelio, LinkedIn-type) for this. The wages are imputed from job titles and firms, so the decomposition you get back is partly built into the imputation.

## My recommendation

1. **Ask your advisor and department first.** Find out who already holds an approved project with IAB, BPLIM, RAIS, LEHD, or Nordic data. Joining an existing project is by far the fastest path for a second-year.
2. **Apply to IAB (LIAB) and BPLIM (QP) now, in parallel.** Both are free, both accept foreign researchers in some form, and both work through remote execution, so you don't have to relocate.
3. **Build your pipeline on the IAB test data and `pytwoway` simulations while you wait.**

Expect several months before you can work with real data. Plan your second-year paper timeline around that.

Sources:
- [FDZ LIAB LM 7521](https://fdz.iab.de/en/int_bd_pd/linked-employer-employee-data-of-the-iab-liab-liab-longitudinal-model-1975-2021-version-1/)
- [FDZ on-site and remote access](https://fdz.iab.de/en/data-access/on-site-use/)
- [MIT Admin Data Handbook, IAB chapter](https://admindatahandbook.mit.edu/book/v1.1/iab.html)
- [BPLIM access](https://bplim.bportugal.pt/content/access-0)
- [BPLIM Guide for Researchers (2018)](https://cicee.autonoma.pt/wp-content/uploads/2024/03/BPlim_Guide_for_Researchers_v2018sep26.pdf)
- [MTE RAIS/CAGED microdata](https://www.gov.br/trabalho-e-emprego/pt-br/acesso-a-informacao/acoes-e-programas/programas-projetos-acoes-obras-e-atividades/estatisticas-trabalho/microdados-rais-e-caged)
- [Identified RAIS application](https://www.gov.br/pt-br/servicos/solicitar-acesso-aos-dados-identificados-rais-e-caged)
- [RAIS pública overview](https://marianahaase.substack.com/p/rais-publica-que-os-micridados-permitem)

- **Why it fits:** It's a huge formal-sector census, popular for AKM and inequality work (e.g., Alvarez et al. 2018).

graders.name: 01-recall-german-iab
graders.evidence:
No public dataset lets you follow workers across employers for 10+ years with real firm identifiers. Every dataset that fits an AKM design is restricted. Some are much easier to get than others, and you can build and test your whole pipeline before you have any of them.

I wrote this from what I know, not from checking each provider's current rules today. Access rules change, so check the details on each provider's website before you plan around them.

## A point about your design

The within/between decomposition (as in Song et al. 2019) only needs firm IDs in each year's cross-section. AKM needs a lot of **movers** inside a connected set, and with few movers per firm you get serious limited-mobility bias in the variance components. So:
- Small worker samples (1–2% of workers) are weak for AKM, because most firms show up with one or two sampled workers.
- Plan to use a bias correction from the start: Kline–Saggio–Sølvsten (2020) leave-out, or the Bonhomme–Lamadon–Manresa clustering approach. Reviewers will expect it.

## The main options, from most to least realistic for a PhD student

**1. Portugal: Quadros de Pessoal (via BPLIM, Banco de Portugal)**
- Mandatory annual census of private-sector employers from the mid-1980s on (a few years are missing). It has worker and firm IDs, which makes it ideal for AKM. Card, Cardoso & Kline (2016, QJE) used it.
- Access: send a project proposal to BPLIM. If approved, you work on their remote server; output is checked before release, and you usually get test data to write code against. It is open to researchers outside Portugal.
- Realistic timeline: a few months from proposal to access. For a non-Portuguese student this is probably the most accessible full-census option.

**2. Germany: IAB data (via the FDZ, the IAB's research data centre)**
- **LIAB** (linked establishment survey and worker records) and **BHP** (establishment panel). The **AKM firm effects estimated by the IAB on the full employment register (IEB)** can be merged onto SIAB/BHP. That means you can study firm effects without estimating AKM on a 2% sample yourself.
- **SIAB** is a 2% worker sample covering decades. It's great for long careers but thin for estimating AKM yourself.
- Access: contract with the FDZ and a short project description. Work is done on-site at FDZ locations (in Germany, plus some at US universities) or by remote execution (JoSuA). You write code against **structure-identical test data you can get early**, then send it to run on the real data.
- Timeline: usually a few months. There is also a scientific-use file (SIAB-R) you can use at your own institution, but check whether it includes establishment IDs and whether your institution qualifies.

**3. Italy: Veneto Worker History (VWH) and INPS**
- VWH covers all private-sector employment in Veneto from the mid-1970s to around 2001 and was used by Card, Devicienti & Maida (2014). It has historically been available through the University of Padova with a signed agreement, which is fairly easy. Check its current status.
- Full national INPS data goes through the VisitINPS program: competitive proposals, with access on-site or remote. It's slower.

**4. Austria: Austrian Social Security Database (ASSD)**
- Full-population employment histories from 1972 with employer IDs. Access usually goes through a collaboration with a University of Linz / Vienna-based project, not an open application. You'd likely need a coauthor or advisor connection.

**5. US: LEHD (Census, via FSRDC)**
- Excellent data, but the hardest route: a full proposal to Census, a background check for Special Sworn Status, work only in an FSRDC, and disclosure review. Expect 6–18 months before you have access. State coverage depends on which states have agreed, and foreign nationals face extra residency requirements. The SSA data Song et al. used is basically not accessible.

**6. Nordic registers (Denmark IDA, Sweden, Norway, Finland FLEED) and the Netherlands (CBS)**
- These are top quality, but access usually has to go through an **authorized domestic institution**. For you that means a coauthor or visiting position there. Finland and the Netherlands (CBS Remote Access) are somewhat more open to foreign institutions, but charge fees.

**7. France (DADS / Panel tous salariés via CASD), UK (ASHE via ONS SRS / UKDS Secure Lab), Canada (CEEDD via StatCan RDCs)**
- All of these are possible. France usually needs a French partner institution, and CASD charges fees. ASHE is a 1% sample, so it's thin for AKM. Canadian access works best if you're at a Canadian university.

**Brazil: RAIS.** The free public RAIS microdata has **no worker or firm identifiers**, so it can't support AKM. The identified version needs an agreement with the Labor Ministry, which is now hard to get.

graders.name: 01-recall-german-iab
graders.evidence:
I answered this from what I already know and didn't check any of the providers' websites today. Access rules, fees and timelines change often, so confirm each one on the provider's site before you plan around it.

## The short answer

- **Easiest real data:** Portugal (*Quadros de Pessoal* through the Banco de Portugal's research lab) and Germany (the IAB's research data centre, the FDZ). Both regularly approve applications from academics at foreign universities. Expect roughly 2–6 months.
- **Hardest:** the US (LEHD), the Nordic registers and identified Brazilian RAIS. They're possible, but it takes a year or more, or a coauthor who already has access.
- **Nothing public works for AKM.** No freely downloadable dataset follows workers across firms with firm identifiers over 10+ years. What you can start on today is simulated data and test files that have the real structure but fake values (details at the end).

## The options, roughly from most to least accessible

### 1. Portugal: Quadros de Pessoal (QP)
- **What it is:** a mandatory annual census of essentially all private-sector employers and their employees, with worker and firm IDs. It runs from the mid-1980s to the present, with a couple of missing years (around 1990 and 2001). Card, Cardoso & Kline (2016, QJE) used it for exactly this kind of decomposition.
- **How to get it:** apply to **BPLIM** (the Banco de Portugal's Microdata Research Laboratory). You send a project proposal, sign confidentiality terms and then work on their remote server. Output is checked before you can take it out.
- **Realistic effort:** a moderate application. They're used to foreign academics, and I believe it's free for academic research (please confirm). Plan for weeks to a few months.
- **Fit:** excellent. It's the full population, so you get enough workers who switch firms to estimate firm effects well.

### 2. Germany: data from the IAB research data centre (FDZ)
- **Products:**
  - **SIAB:** a 2% sample of workers with their full employment histories.
  - **LIAB:** linked employer-employee data built around the IAB Establishment Panel.
  - **SIEED:** a sample of establishments with the complete employment histories of everyone who worked there.
  - Full administrative data (the IEB, which Card, Heining & Kline 2013 used): only by special arrangement.
- **How to get it:**
  - You need a non-commercial research institution and an approved project, then a usage contract.
  - Most linked data can only be used on-site, at FDZ locations in Germany or at partner sites abroad (several have been at US universities; check the current list), or by remote execution, where you send code and get back checked output.
  - A less detailed SIAB file can be used at your own university.
  - It's free for academics, and approval usually takes a few months.
- **Fit:**
  - SIEED and LIAB suit AKM much better than SIAB. In a 2% worker sample, most firms have too few movers, and the firm effects come out badly biased (limited-mobility bias).
  - The FDZ also offers **ready-made AKM worker and firm effects** estimated on the full administrative data (FDZ Method Report 01/2020, Bellmann et al.). You can merge these onto its other datasets, which partly gets around the sampling problem.

### 3. France: DADS / Panel Tous Salariés
- **How to get it:** through **CASD**. You first need accreditation from the *Comité du secret statistique*, and then you work remotely through a special access terminal (the SD-Box).
- **Realistic effort:**
  - There are real fees: CASD charges per project per year, and it's usually your institution that pays.
  - It's much easier from a French institution or with a French coauthor.
  - Plan for 6+ months.
- **Fit:** good, long history. The panel samples workers, so firm effects run into the same thin-sample issue as SIAB, though the full-population establishment files help.

### 4. Italy
- **INPS administrative data:** the VisitINPS Scholars programme takes competitive project applications, and you work on-site in Rome or remotely. It's a real option but selective.
- **Veneto Worker History (VWH, 1975–2001):** used by Card, Devicienti & Maida. It has historically been easier to get, on request from the University of Padova/Venice group, but I'm not sure of its current status. It ends in 2001 and covers only one region.

### 5. Austria: Austrian Social Security Database (ASSD)
Excellent data going back decades. In practice you usually get access by working with the labour economics group at JKU Linz, which is a coauthor route rather than an application.

### 6. UK: ASHE panel
- **What it is:** a 1% sample of workers, with employer identifiers and a long history (from 1975 if you include the earlier NES survey).
- **How to get it:** become an ONS Accredited Researcher (a training course plus a project application), then work through the ONS Secure Research Service or the UK Data Service SecureLab. It's easiest from a UK institution.
- **Fit:** the 1% sample makes firm effects weak.

### 7. US: LEHD
- **How to get it:** through a Federal Statistical Research Data Center. You submit a proposal through the Standard Application Process; Census reviews it, often for 6–12+ months; and you need Special Sworn Status, which includes a background check and residency requirements for non-citizens.
- **Other conditions:**
  - You must work physically at an RDC, and many charge fees unless your university is a member.
  - Every output goes through disclosure review.
  - Which states are covered depends on each state's approval.
- **Fit:** great, but it's a 1–2 year commitment. The SSA earnings data used in Song et al. (2019) is effectively unavailable.

### 8. Brazil: RAIS
- **Identified RAIS** has been the workhorse for this literature (e.g., Alvarez, Benguria, Engbom & Moser 2018). But it requires an agreement with the Ministry of Labour, and Brazil's data protection law (LGPD) has made that harder. In practice people mostly get in through existing agreements or coauthors.
- **The public RAIS microdata** are free to download, but they **don't include persistent worker identifiers**, so you can't follow movers. They're useless for AKM.

### 9. Nordic countries and Canada
- **Denmark, Sweden, Norway, Finland:** fantastic register data, but you generally need to be affiliated with an authorised institution in that country, and there are fees. It's realistic only with a local coauthor or a research visit.
- **Canada:** CEEDD through Statistics Canada's research data centres. Same story.

## What you can start this week

1. **Simulated data with known worker and firm effects.** `pytwoway` (Bonhomme, Lamadon et al.) has a simulator plus AKM, KSS-corrected and BLM estimators. For KSS there's also the authors' MATLAB code and a Julia package (`VarianceComponentsHDFE`); in Stata, `reghdfe`. Writing the full pipeline now means you can run it as soon as you get access. That matters most where you'll be working on a remote server or sending code by remote execution:
   - building the connected set (and the leave-one-out connected set)
   - estimation
   - the bias correction for limited mobility
   - the variance decomposition over time
2. **FDZ test files.** The FDZ publishes test versions of its datasets with the real structure and fake values. You can write your actual cleaning code against them.
3. **Start a proposal right away.** My recommendation is BPLIM (Portugal) as the main application, plus an FDZ application for SIEED or LIAB with the ready-made AKM effects. Both are realistic for a second-year student. Running them at the same time protects you against delays.
4. **Ask your advisor and department.** Find out whether anyone already has an LEHD, RAIS, CASD or Nordic project you could join. That's often the fastest way into the restricted datasets.

One last point that matters whichever dataset you use: with plain AKM, the share of wage variance attributed to firms is badly biased upward when firms have few movers. Use KSS or BLM corrections, and expect referees to ask for them.

- **Realistic effort:** a moderate application. They're used to foreign academics, and I believe it's free for academic research (please confirm). Plan for weeks to a few months.
- **Fit:** excellent. It's the full population, so you get enough workers who switch firms to estimate firm effects well.

### 2. Germany: data from the IAB research data centre (FDZ)
- **Products:**
  - **SIAB:** a 2% sample of workers with their full employment histories.
  - **LIAB:** linked employer-employee data built around the IAB Establishment Panel.
  - **SIEED:** a sample of establishments with the complete employment histories of everyone who worked there.
  - Full administrative data (the IEB, which Card, Heining & Kline 2013 used): only by special arrangement.
- **How to get it:**
  - You need a non-commercial research institution and an approved project, then a usage contract.
  - Most linked data can only be used on-site, at FDZ locations in Germany or at partner sites abroad (several have been at US universities; check the current list), or by remote execution, where you send code and get back checked output.
  - A less detailed SIAB file can be used at your own university.
  - It's free for academics, and approval usually takes a few months.
- **Fit:**
  - SIEED and LIAB suit AKM much better than SIAB. In a 2% worker sample, most firms have too few movers, and the firm effects come out badly biased (limited-mobility bias).
  - The FDZ also offers **ready-made AKM worker and firm effects** estimated on the full administrative data (FDZ Method Report 01/2020, Bellmann et al.). You can merge these onto its other datasets, which partly gets around the sampling problem.

### 3. France: DADS / Panel Tous Salariés
- **How to get it:** through **CASD**. You first need accreditation from the *Comité du secret statistique*, and then you work remotely through a special access terminal (the SD-Box).
- **Realistic effort:**
  - There are real fees: CASD charges per project per year, and it's usually your institution that pays.
  - It's much easier from a French institution or with a French coauthor.
  - Plan for 6+ months.
- **Fit:** good, long history. The panel samples workers, so firm effects run into the same thin-sample issue as SIAB, though the full-population establishment files help.

### 4. Italy
- **INPS administrative data:** the VisitINPS Scholars programme takes competitive project applications, and you work on-site in Rome or remotely. It's a real option but selective.
- **Veneto Worker History (VWH, 1975–2001):** used by Card, Devicienti & Maida. It has historically been easier to get, on request from the University of Padova/Venice group, but I'm not sure of its current status. It ends in 2001 and covers only one region.

### 5. Austria: Austrian Social Security Database (ASSD)
Excellent data going back decades. In practice you usually get access by working with the labour economics group at JKU Linz, which is a coauthor route rather than an application.

### 6. UK: ASHE panel
- **What it is:** a 1% sample of workers, with employer identifiers and a long history (from 1975 if you include the earlier NES survey).
- **How to get it:** become an ONS Accredited Researcher (a training course plus a project application), then work through the ONS Secure Research Service or the UK Data Service SecureLab. It's easiest from a UK institution.
- **Fit:** the 1% sample makes firm effects weak.

### 7. US: LEHD
- **How to get it:** through a Federal Statistical Research Data Center. You submit a proposal through the Standard Application Process; Census reviews it, often for 6–12+ months; and you need Special Sworn Status, which includes a background check and residency requirements for non-citizens.
- **Other conditions:**
  - You must work physically at an RDC, and many charge fees unless your university is a member.
  - Every output goes through disclosure review.
  - Which states are covered depends on each state's approval.
- **Fit:** great, but it's a 1–2 year commitment. The SSA earnings data used in Song et al. (2019) is effectively unavailable.

### 8. Brazil: RAIS
- **Identified RAIS** has been the workhorse for this literature (e.g., Alvarez, Benguria, Engbom & Moser 2018). But it requires an agreement with the Ministry of Labour, and Brazil's data protection law (LGPD) has made that harder. In practice people mostly get in through existing agreements or coauthors.
- **The public RAIS microdata** are free to download, but they **don't include persistent worker identifiers**, so you can't follow movers. They're useless for AKM.

### 9. Nordic countries and Canada
- **Denmark, Sweden, Norway, Finland:** fantastic register data, but you generally need to be affiliated with an authorised institution in that country, and there are fees. It's realistic only with a local coauthor or a research visit.
- **Canada:** CEEDD through Statistics Canada's research data centres. Same story.

## What you can start this week

1. **Simulated data with known worker and firm effects.** `pytwoway` (Bonhomme, Lamadon et al.) has a simulator plus AKM, KSS-corrected and BLM estimators. For KSS there's also the authors' MATLAB code and a Julia package (`VarianceComponentsHDFE`); in Stata, `reghdfe`. Writing the full pipeline now means you can run it as soon as you get access. That matters most where you'll be working on a remote server or sending code by remote execution:
   - building the connected set (and the leave-one-out connected set)
   - estimation
   - the bias correction for limited mobility
   - the variance decomposition over time
2. **FDZ test files.** The FDZ publishes test versions of its datasets with the real structure and fake values. You can write your actual cleaning code against them.
3. **Start a proposal right away.** My recommendation is BPLIM (Portugal) as the main application, plus an FDZ application for SIEED or LIAB with the ready-made AKM effects. Both are realistic for a second-year student. Running them at the same time protects you against delays.
4. **Ask your advisor and department.** Find out whether anyone already has an LEHD, RAIS, CASD or Nordic project you could join. That's often the fastest way into the restricted datasets.

One last point that matters whichever dataset you use: with plain AKM, the share of wage variance attributed to firms is badly biased upward when firms have few movers. Use KSS or BLM corrections, and expect referees to ask for them.
